lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Calls this meeting to order. Good evening, everyone. Welcome to this meeting. And at this time, I would like to give the opening to Councillor Damian Penner.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mayor. Go Canada, go! Yeah, currently we are right in the middle of the Winter Olympics, and with just under a week left for Canada to go for gold, the Olympics And as a proud Canadian, specifically the Winter Olympics is an exciting time that harbors a sense of national pride, unity, and optimism. We as Canadians get to watch the pinnacle of human ability on showcase for a once-in-4-years opportunity for these athletes to have the lifelong bragging rights of being an Olympic champion. And as a nation, we unite behind the Maple Leaf, and regardless of the athlete's views, Thank you. political associations, religion, or race. We cheer for them simply because they are Canadian. While I am currently in my glory spending far too much time in front of the TV, on my phone, a tablet, sometimes all 3 all at the same time, to immerse myself in the spectacle that is the Winter Olympics, it gave me pause to consider our national unity. Canada is not the same country it was 10 years ago, and 10 years from now it will not be the same country we live in Demographics change, governments change, and even what may or not be socially acceptable changes. That is a reality of the world we live in, and the fact that change happens must be accepted. We do not always have to accept the particular— that the particular change is for the better, but denying that it will happen is a fool's errand. One thing that we can never change if we want to continue to see our nation grow prosperous is our national pride. I'm admittedly not familiar with the current social studies curricular, but coming up in school, we were all taught that Canada was a cultural mosaic, mosaic where different cultures from across the world come together to create a beautifully— a beautiful country working in harmony towards the greater good of the nation. A mosaic where each beautiful culture represents a color, and only when they are all stitched together working in unity can you stand back and see the beauty that the mosaic is. While I still believe that working together towards a common goal is our nature as Canadians, we can do better. Let's do the Canadian thing and accept each other's differences, but more importantly, focus and celebrate all the things we have in common that creates the whole mosaic and unite behind the maple leaf as a nation. In 2000, Molson put out a now famous commercial that you may, may remember titled My Name Is Joe. And I am Canadian. It was a tongue-in-cheek shot at Americans for the purpose of selling Canadian beer, but it really doesn't get more Canuck than that— cracking a cold one and taking some cheap shots at our neighbour. It was a commercial that talked about what makes us Canadian, with lines like, I speak English and French, not American, and I pronounce it about, not aboot. And I don't live in an igloo or eat blubber or own a dog sled. And how about this gem? I don't know Jimmy, Sally, or Susie from Canada, although I am certain they're really, really nice. Beer, the great uniter of a nation's people. Well, the Olympics is an international event that brings the world together, and I hope that this momentum of national pride continues beyond the extinguishing of the Olympic torch. I was also touched last week when I saw during the Tumbler Ridge Memorial for the tragedy that occurred there The leaders of all the main political parties holding hands in solidarity for the families and the community. They put aside their partisan ways and looked at each other as a Canadian and nothing else. That is what it truly means to be a Canadian. These moments of national unity cannot be once every 2 years during the Olympics or when a national tragedy occurs, but need to be a day— daily— but need to be daily and intentional. Thank you. It all starts with each of us taking ownership of the great nation we live in and doing better each day with the way we interact with others. We need leaders in business and politics that put the value in building relationships regardless of the differences. We need to elect individuals that focus on collaboration for the Canadian good and not division to appease a certain group of individuals. Canada needs to embrace relationship-driven leadership again and work across lines to get the results we need so our nation can bring home the gold on the world stage again. Thank you, Mr. Mayor.

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I'm not quite sure how much to summarize. It's a quite lengthy report. Suffice it to say, the city has contracted with WSP Canada or its predecessors for at least the past 20 years in doing annual traffic count analysis within the city of Steinbach on both Yes. The PTH 12 and also the PTH 52 traffic corridors in Steinbach. This year's traffic count review was conducted and looked at 20 specific intersections along those traffic corridors. That is noted in the introduction of the document. On page 15 of the document and 27 of council's agenda package, there is a summary as to the observed peak hour traffic volumes that were counted at these various intersections in Steinbach, with the most heavily traveled route being at the intersection of PTH 52 and PTH 12 or Main Street. Yes. Reaching nearly 3,500 vehicles per hour. That is significant, and the overall year-over-year growth and long-term growth of traffic has tended to follow a general pattern of increasing over, over the several years that, that the city has conducted the study. In addition to overall traffic counts and the The identification of trends. The traffic analysis also looks at traffic movements at these various intersections, both signalized and unsignalized. And what this information or what this research does is provides the city with valuable insight and trending analysis to determine which intersections are prime candidates for— Thank you. No action, and more importantly, which intersections are prime candidates for further action or improvements to address the overall volumes of traffic. As I mentioned earlier, as the city of Steinbach grows, the overall level of traffic activity in Steinbach, and especially among its main thoroughfares, has increased over time. At the end of the report, there are Summaries as to some of the trends that were observed, and more importantly, the consultant has indicated a few recommendations for the city to consider at some point in the future. And again, these recommendations are exactly that; they aren't they aren't must-haves. However, based on the actual observed conditions. for the opportunity to speak to the report and the activities. These are recommendations that administration does take into account every year as it recommends capital programming to City Council for consideration. But for example, and very briefly, and it's found in section 4.3 of the report, it indicates the 3 main recommendations. Yes. The consultant recommends that the city implement traffic signals at the intersection of PTH 52 West and Giesbrecht Street in 2026. That was an intersection that had been recommended for signalization in several previous reports, but as that physical project appears to be now imminent, there are no further comments related to that. Secondly, the consultant recommends that traffic volumes and operations at the intersection of PTH 52 and Lund Road be monitored or continue to be monitored going forward as traffic movements there to a degree indicate that perhaps signalization could be considered there. However, that is subject to further review and consideration of city council in the future. And finally, the report suggests that the Okay. Timing plan on PTH 12 North at Clearspring Centre and Golfair Road, PTH 12 North at Park Road East and West, and PTH 12 North at the Superstore and co-op access could see improved operations and improvements in critical movements by adjusting the timing plan and the splits. And that would be subject to further analysis with— along with MTI, who is the authority who manages all the traffic signalization in Steinbach. Other than that, if— unless there are some questions of council, that concludes my comments on this report. And recommendation is that council accept the report as presented.

lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Just to note that on page 9 of the report, it actually tells us how long we've been doing these traffic counts. Since 1997. So happy 29th anniversary of our traffic study. I think this is an example of the foresight of past councils because this started long before any of us had ever run for council, of having this done annually. We have data that we're able to present to the province to show that our growth does merit improvements to our intersections. And we've seen a lot of changes over the last, you know, 5, 10, 15 years, a lot of upgrades. The most recent one, the most significant one, of course, is the, the new intersection that we have at PTH 12 and Loewen Boulevard. I do want to point out that in regards to the recommendations here, these are important. I completely agree with you, Mr. Mayor, that we need to Advocate to the province to ensure that the lights actually do go at the 52 West and Giesbrecht Street intersection. This has been promised for years and the province keeps moving that. And so we need to remind the province that there's a— that they've made a commitment to put those lights in and those traffic signals need to be put in. And so I do think we need to follow up there. I certainly do agree with monitoring traffic volumes at the intersection of PTH 52 West and Lund Road. Because we need to see what the impact of our new intersection is. Like, we're obviously— we need to see how traffic patterns change now that we've fully upgraded PTH 12 and Loewen Boulevard. I also agree with the— we need to ask the province about adjusting the timing of the lights along PTH 12. This is a— it's a point of frustration for many of us over many years that the lights never seem to be properly synchronized. And now that we've done these upgrades along Highway 12. We should have the— we should be able to get these synchronized, at least I would certainly hope so. So I, I think it's good that we do this study. It gives us data, it gives us evidence, and I think this really helps us with advocating for the improvements that we want to see. So I'm really glad that councils from years ago started this, and I think we should continue with these reports.

lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. It is no secret that, uh, we've had some drainage challenges in Steinbach in the past couple of years with 2 major rainfalls that have caused extensive flooding across the city. And so this is a small part of, um, amping up the capacity our lift stations have run water through our city and get it draining more quickly. This is only one project. I know, Council, we've also been talking about other projects that we can do to alleviate potential flooding again. So this is a good first step, and I'm happy to be able to make the motion for it. As, you know, as we all know, this flooding has significantly impacted our— the neighborhood I'm in.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you. Anything further?

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mayor. This is a low tender that came in just under $1.5 million. The engineer's estimate was $2.4 million. This is a substantial savings to the taxpayers, partnered with the fact that we have a grant for a portion of this. This is one of the aspects of the larger— the larger project that's going to be along Park Road West with increased pumping capacity at the lift station as well as facility upgrades with a total project estimate of $7.4 million. But it's good that the beginning, the first tender on this larger project came in under budget. So hopefully we can see the savings on the rest of the tenders as well.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further, council? Anything in closing?

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Nothing further.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Yes, council, this has been a project that's been on the books for a long time, and I'm so glad we're doing it because this will increase capacity For the entire city. This is something that will help every property in our city. It'll help, it'll facilitate more growth. And this is the one component. The other component is the lift station upgrade that will also increase capacity as well. I think those are 2 projects that need to be done in tandem and really looking forward to getting them both done this year. So call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. So move into administration. We've got 9A, accounts payable, back of the book. We've all had a chance to review. Looking for a motion to approve. So moved. Second. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. We've got 4451/2025/9210. This is referring to 905 Main Street. It's by resolution. Mr. Warkentin, could you please introduce this file?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. The file number you quoted is the subdivision application file number, the 905 Main Street in Steinbach. The application for Okay. Application for subdivision has been submitted by [name withheld] on behalf of the registered owner, 10225445 Manitoba Limited. Purpose of the subdivision application is to subdivide the subject property into— from a single lot into 4 parcels. The subject property is designated as residential policy area under the city's official Community Plan and is zoned RRS, which is rural residential service, pursuant to Steinbach Zoning Bylaw 2245. There is public sewer available for all of the newly created lots with the existing house on the subject property currently being connected to the city's gravity sewer system. It is recommended that council approve the application under this subdivision, uh, file subject to the execution of development agreement.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Ward. Um, council, how would you like to proceed?

lines.speaker: Jake Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jake Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Motion to approve.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Seconded by Councillor Penner. Go ahead, Councillor Hiebert.

lines.speaker: Jake Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jake Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. The applicant here is requesting a somewhat complicated subdivision in which they're dividing A single lot into 3 new lots plus the resulting 4th lot that's there already. On this one, I want to make note that MIT has indicated that there'll be no new approaches that be permitted along Main Street, so lots 3 and 4 are required to have a shared driveway. Thank you. Then other than that, the size of the lots meet our zoning bylaws, so I'm in favor of agreeing to this one. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further?

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Nothing further.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further of council? Anything in closing?

lines.speaker: Jake Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jake Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Nothing, thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Council, we have 9C, the building permits for January 2026. That is on page 86. Council, how would you like to proceed? Councillor Zwaagstra.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Motion to approve.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Seconded by Councillor Hiebert. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I'm glad to have support on the building permits. Just over $4 million in building permits issued in the month of January. That is a good start for the year. January is typically Typically is one of the slower months because, of course, it's in the middle of winter. And $1.7 million in residential and basically a variety of some single-family dwellings, finished basements and such. And then, of course, we also have commercial and industrial at $2.6 million and things such as warehouses and storage and all that. And of course, each one of those adds up. And so I look forward to seeing what happens in 2026, I think 2025 is a strong year, and with just over $4.3 million in building permits in January, I think we're off to a good start.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further?

lines.speaker: Jake Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jake Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Nothing further, thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further for council? Anything in closing? No. Council, I agree. $4.3 million is a good start for a cold January. Call for the question. All those in favour? Opposed? That is carried. We have the business tax and 2025 small balances cancellations. Council, this is, this is more of a housekeeping, a housekeeping item that we do this every year. These are some, some businesses that either closed or moved or there's write-offs that have happened. So it's just a matter of acknowledging these and, and writing them off the books. Looking for a motion to approve. Councillor Susan Penner, seconded by Councillor Siemens. Any comments? No. Well, call for the question. All those in favour? Opposed? That is carried. We have 9E. This is the realty tax cancellations. So these 2, we're just making Making a motion to make our books line up. It's, again, it's housekeeping. Council? Motion to approve.

lines.speaker: Jake Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jake Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Motion to approve.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Councillor Hiebert, second by Councillor Penner. No comments. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. We've got 9F. This is rezoning bylaw 2253. This is referring to 41st Street This is the third reading. Mr. Warkentin, could you please introduce this file?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Just one moment as I—

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Been a while since we've seen this file.

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: It has been a while. I just wanted to bring up details, but that is correct. Bylaw 2253 was considered by council at the public hearing several months ago. The applicant has continued to provide administration with the required documentation and information so that the file can be brought forward. That has now gotten to the point where a development agreement has been prepared and has been signed by the applicant. As such, all of the conditions that are required for this rezoning application have mostly been completed. This now brings us to this step where recommendation from administration is for council to give Bylaw 2253, which was rezoning the subject property from RLD residential low density RMD residential medium density to complete third reading, and recommendation is for council to do so subject to the execution of this development agreement.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Orkney. Council, how would you like to proceed? Councillor Siemens?

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Motion to approve.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Seconded by Councillor Penner. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is an application for— to build a multifamily unit on the corner of First Street and Giesbrecht. This is a unique building. We don't have one of these in Steinbach currently. The building takes up majority of the lot, and the parking will be directly under the building, but it won't be enclosed parking. It'll be— so the 3 stories will be elevated with parking underneath. So we haven't seen one of those before in Steinbach. But this is a multifamily, and it fits into— on First Street with a lot of the other multifamily that we have. It's close to industrial Close to walkability, and this is the, the third and final reading, so we can maybe move this project ahead.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further?

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Yeah, I concur. This project fits in with the neighborhood. There's been a lot of redevelopment on First Street, which has been really nice to see. This is also a really efficient use of land with having the parking under and the units on top. So I'm looking forward to seeing this project go forward.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further, council? Anything closing? Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Got 9G. We've got business licenses. We've got, uh, 2 pages and a little bit of business licenses. Looking for a motion to approve. Councillor Penner. Second by Councillor Zwaagstra, go ahead.

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mayor. These are annual renewals of businesses that either operate within Steinbach boundary or boundary as non-resident, or are residents operating businesses out of their homes, not necessarily needing commercial space. So this is them doing their due diligence and getting licenses from the city to operate those businesses.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor) [medium]
lines.text: Anything further?

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: That covered it.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further, council? Closing?

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Not often I can get Councillor Zwaagstra speechless, so.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Call for the question. All those in favour? Opposed? That is carried. This one will be tough to get through without Bill here, but we've got excavator licenses on page 101. Looking for a motion to approve. Councillor Siemens. On

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Behalf of Bill— on behalf of Bill Hiebert.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Any comments? Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. We are at council question period. Are there any questions of council? Okay. We've got correspondence and petitions. We've got the 11A Jake Epp Library. This is amendments of December 10th, 2025. Council, would you like to proceed, take it as information?

lines.speaker: Damian Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Damian Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: Please.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay. And we've got 11B. This is a letter from [name withheld], a request for signage. Council, whether we— whether we do this, whether we, like, we'll take it as information, whether we do do any signage or not, one thing I do want to ask Deputy Mayor, Councillor Michael Zwaagstra, we are meeting with the RCMP advisory. I'm thinking there maybe needs to be a little bit of policing done on this street if there's that kind of speeds and that kind of pedestrian traffic there.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Yep, we can add it to the agenda. We have a meeting tomorrow, so.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, good. Then, Councillor Zwaagstra, we'll take this up with our RCMP advisory. and try and get some feedback from them and see if there's something we can do with a little bit of patrolling or policing in that area. Otherwise, take it as information at this time. Okay, thank you. We'll take it as information. There's no other business. Looking for a motion to adjourn. Councillor Penner. Second by Councillor Hiebert. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Next regular council meeting is Tuesday, March 3rd, 2026 at 7:30.
